sourceLine: your PlaneVR and ImmersiveXR work, and the questions training leads ask before they buy VR

cards.title: Flight School VR: Measure Time to Solo
cards.angle: Boeing's 2026 outlook calls for 674,000 new pilots worldwide by 2045, and two-thirds of that demand replaces retirees. VR procedural training only pays off if it frees aircraft and instructor time, so judge it on hours to solo, not novelty.
cards.evidence: Your Learn2Fly testimonial reports a student who went solo in 10.7 hours against a usual 13.0. Your PlaneVR page claims a 15% bottom-line gain. Both rest on one school's account and your own estimate, so show the method before the number.

cards.title: OEM Training in VR: Induct Without Shutdowns
cards.angle: Konecranes adopted a VR crane simulator in May 2026 to expand training capacity and cut equipment downtime. Packaging VR with equipment lets customers induct users without stopping the plant, and lets sales demo features around the clock.
cards.evidence: Your ImmersiveXR builds from a customer's CAD, scans or generative AI models. It covers shutdown, maintenance and full-system training. The page names no OEM client, so confirm one before writing a case. Your 2023 OEM induction article exists, so this is a refresh.

cards.title: Defence XR Training: Plan the Device Fleet
cards.angle: Samsung added Android Enterprise to Galaxy XR, with Knox security and managed app deployment for training and manufacturing. Defence buyers need managed fleets, controlled updates and security review designed in from day one.
cards.evidence: Your site cites nine years working with the Australian Defence Force and delivery in ten countries. It names no projects, so get approved detail before writing from it.
